newsitem.title: UK: Venezuela's Bitor disappointed at UK plant closure.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Bitor disappointed at UK plant closure.

text.p: Venezuelan company Bitor said on Wednesday it was disappointed that PowerGen Plc had decided to close a British power plant that burns its Orimulsion fuel.

PowerGen, Britain's second biggest power generator, said it was closing its 500 megawatt Ince power station in northwest England, which burns about one million tonnes of Orimulsion a year under a five-year contract.
To make up for the loss of power, PowerGen said it was bringing back into operation a generating unit at Fiddler's Ferry power station, also in northwest England.
Bitor Europe Ltd said in a statement: "We are disappointed to hear the news and especially regret the job losses that will be associated with it, including those involved in the fuel delivery.

"We understand that the decision is simply one of saving overheads -- obviously it is cheaper to run a spare 500 MW unit at an operating power station than a stand alone 500 MW power station such as Ince."
"Orimulsion's future in the U.K. will be in larger, better located plant that fully meets New Plant Standards.
"We accept that PowerGen did not plan to make the necessary investments at Ince to achieve these standards and thus the future life of the power station was limited," it added.
Bitor said the five-year programme at Ince was a long-term technical trial that was "completely successful."
Industry sources said the decision to close Ince came as a surprise to Bitor.
The company is negotiating with PowerGen's larger rival, National Power Plc, to burn four to five million tonnes a year of Orimulsion at Pembroke power station in south Wales.
The government is yet to approve plans to convert the currently mothballed plant to burning Orimulsion.

Orimulsion consists of bitumen, found in huge quantities in Venezuela's Orinoco Belt, dispersed in 26 to 30 percent water, plus a small amount of chemical surfactant to prevent the oil and water from separating. --Michael Rank, London newsroom +44 171 542 7629
